grupos.objetivo: Order a coffee and something to eat politely with «queria», count from 20 to 100, understand prices in reais and ask how much it is.
Ask and tell the time, name the days of the week and the months, say today's date and arrange when something happens.
Use «estar» to say how you feel and where people and things are, choose between «ser» and «estar», and use the contractions «no, na, nos, nas, do, da, dos, das» with places.
Ask where a place is with «onde fica…?», understand and give simple directions (straight, left, right, until the traffic light) and say how to get somewhere and how long it takes.
Use the present tense of ir, fazer, poder, ver, vir, dizer, pôr, saber and conhecer to say where you go, what you do, what you can do, what you see and say, and to tell «saber» from «conhecer».

grupos.titulo: Wanting, being able to, needing and having to
grupos.objetivo: Say what you want, what you can or may do, what you need and what you have to do, ask for permission and ask politely for help or for a repetition.
Describe your day from waking up to going to bed, say at what time you do things and how often, and use reflexive verbs such as «levantar-se» and «vestir-se» correctly.
Name clothes and colors, point at things with «este, esse, aquele», ask the price, say your size and buy something in a shop.

grupos.titulo: Likes and preferences: gostar and preferir
grupos.objetivo: Say what you like, love, dislike and prefer, ask other people about their tastes, and agree or disagree with «eu também» and «eu também não».

grupos.titulo: Plans and actions in progress: ir + infinitive and estar + gerund
grupos.objetivo: Talk about your plans with «ir + infinitive», say what you are doing right now with «estar + gerund», and handle a short phone call to say where you are and when you arrive.

Review all of A1 in one map, practice reading, listening, speaking and writing with a self-check list, correct the most common mistakes of English speakers and take an original scored mock test covering lessons 1 to 17.

Say what you did yesterday, last week or last year with regular -ar, -er and -ir verbs in the «pretérito perfeito», ask about other people's past actions and spell the verbs that change in the «eu» form (chegar, começar, almoçar).

Use the irregular forms of the simple past (ser/ir, ter, estar, fazer, dizer, poder, querer, saber, pôr, ver, vir, dar, trazer) to tell what happened, where you went and what you did, in real conversations.

grupos.titulo: The imperfect: how things used to be
grupos.objetivo: Form the imperfect (pretérito imperfeito) of regular verbs and of the four irregular ones (ser, ter, vir, pôr), and use it to describe your childhood, past habits, people, places, age, time and weather.

grupos.titulo: Simple past or imperfect: telling a story
grupos.objetivo: Choose between the pretérito perfeito (what happened) and the imperfeito (the background, habits and actions in progress), combine them in a story, and understand verbs whose meaning changes (soube/sabia, quis/queria, conheci/conhecia).
Replace a noun with a direct object pronoun (me, te, o, a, nos, os, as), put it in the right place, and answer questions such as «Você viu a Ana?» without repeating the noun.

Say who receives something or who you tell, ask, show or send something to («ele me mandou», «eu te falei», «dei pra ela»), using the spoken forms of Brazil and recognizing the written forms «lhe» and «lhes».

grupos.titulo: Pronoun placement and the spoken norm
grupos.objetivo: Put object pronouns in the right place in spoken Brazilian Portuguese («eu te vi», «vou te ligar», «me dá») and recognize the written forms with a hyphen («vi-o», «vê-lo», «dê-me»).
Compare people, places, prices and options («mais barato do que», «tão rápido quanto», «melhor», «pior») and say which one is the best or the cheapest («o mais barato da cidade», «baratíssimo»).

grupos.titulo: The future: ir + infinitive and the simple future
grupos.objetivo: Talk about plans, promises and predictions with «vou falar» and with the simple future («falarei», «fará», «choverá»), and know when each one is used in speech and in writing.
Give instructions, directions and invitations with the imperative («vire à esquerda», «entre», «fique à vontade», «não se preocupe») and understand the spoken forms of Brazil («fala», «vem», «olha»).
Ask for things, information and help politely («eu queria», «gostaria de», «você poderia me ajudar?»), give advice with «deveria», and accept or refuse a request kindly.

grupos.titulo: Estar + gerund, acabar de, continuar, ficar
grupos.objetivo: Say what is happening now or was happening, say that something has just happened («acabar de»), that it goes on, starts or stops («continuar», «começar a», «parar de»), and use «ficar» to stay, to say where a place is and to say how you feel.

Choose between «por» and «para» in everyday sentences: say what something is for, where you are going, who it is for, thank someone for something, say how long, by what means and for how much, and ask and answer «por que?».

Join two sentences into one with «que», «onde», «quem» and «preposition + que», describe people, things and places in detail («o amigo que mora em Recife», «a cidade onde moro») and explain a word you do not know.

grupos.titulo: Health: the doctor and the pharmacy
grupos.objetivo: Name the parts of the body, say what hurts and what symptoms you have, say for how long, make a doctor's appointment, understand the doctor's questions and instructions and ask for a medicine at the pharmacy.

grupos.titulo: Travel: airport, bus station and hotel
grupos.objetivo: Handle the main travel situations in Brazil: check in at the airport and find your gate, buy a long-distance bus ticket at the «rodoviária», and check in at a hotel, asking the usual questions and understanding the answers.

grupos.titulo: Work and talking about your job
grupos.objetivo: Say what you do for a living, where and for whom you work and how long you have been doing it, give your working hours and make simple requests to colleagues.
Make and answer phone calls, send short WhatsApp messages, invite someone, accept or decline politely and book, confirm or change an appointment.
Describe where you live and the rooms of a home, ask the right questions when renting an apartment, understand prices and costs, and talk politely to neighbors about everyday problems.

Review everything from lessons 19 to 37 on one map, practice reading, listening, speaking and short writing at A2 level, check your own progress with a self-check list and take an original scored simulado with explained answers.

grupos.titulo: Mais-que-perfeito: the past before the past
grupos.objetivo: Say that something had already happened before another moment in the past, explain reasons and surprises in a story, and recognize the simple forms found in written texts.

grupos.titulo: Pretérito perfeito composto and the Brazilian use
grupos.objetivo: Form the pretérito perfeito composto (tenho + participle), understand why in Brazil it means a repeated or continuing action up to now and not the English «have done», and choose the right tense for each situation.
Form the futuro do pretérito (the «would» tense, endings -ia, -ias, -ia, -íamos, -iam) to make polite requests, give advice, say what you would do and talk about imagined or possible situations.

Understand the subjunctive as the mood for what is not (yet) a fact, and form the present subjunctive of regular verbs, of verbs with irregular «eu» forms and of the twelve key irregulars: ser, estar, ter, ir, fazer, ver, vir, dar, saber, querer, poder, haver.

grupos.titulo: The subjunctive: wish, doubt and emotion
grupos.objetivo: Use the present subjunctive after verbs and expressions of wish, request, doubt, possibility, emotion and necessity, and choose correctly between the subjunctive and the indicative (achar que × não achar que).

grupos.titulo: The subjunctive: purpose, time limits and conditions
grupos.objetivo: Use the conjunctions that always take the subjunctive (para que, antes que, até que, sem que, caso, embora, mesmo que, desde que, a menos que) and choose between them and the infinitive when the subject does not change.

Form the imperfect subjunctive (falasse, comesse, partisse, tivesse, fosse, fizesse, viesse…) and use it after wishes, requests and doubts that lie in the past, after «como se» and in the first conditional sentences with «se».

Form the future subjunctive (for, puder, tiver, quiser, fizer, vier, vir, houver…) and use it after «quando», «assim que», «depois que», «sempre que», «enquanto», «se» and «quem/o que/onde» to talk about future events and possibilities.

Talk about possible conditions («se eu puder, eu vou»), unreal hypotheses in the present («se eu tivesse tempo, eu viajaria») and impossible ones in the past («se eu tivesse estudado, teria passado»), and give advice with «no seu lugar».
Report what someone said, asked or requested («ela disse que estava cansada», «ele perguntou se eu morava aqui», «pediu que eu esperasse»), adjusting tenses, pronouns and time words.

Form the passive with «ser» + participle («o prédio foi construído em 1950»), read and write the «se» constructions of signs and formal texts («aluga-se», «precisa-se de»), and know which form to choose in speech and in writing.

Form and use the personal infinitive («para nós fazermos», «sem eles saberem»), know when spoken Portuguese avoids it, and use the gerund and the participle correctly («aprendi vendo filmes», «terminada a aula, saímos»).

grupos.titulo: Relatives (2): cujo, o qual, quanto, onde
grupos.objetivo: Link sentences with «cujo» («o escritor cujo livro li»), «o qual» and prepositions («a casa na qual moro», «a pessoa com quem falei») and with «quanto», «onde / aonde» and «o que» («tudo o que eu quero»), in writing and in speech.

Link ideas with the right connector: contrast and concession («embora», «mesmo que», «no entanto»), cause, consequence and condition («já que», «portanto», «desde que», «senão»), and addition, sequence and conclusion («além disso», «por fim», «em resumo»).
Give your opinion, agree and disagree politely, concede a point, structure an argument with examples and take part in a friendly debate in Brazilian Portuguese.
Address people formally with «o senhor» and «a senhora», write a clear formal e-mail from greeting to closing, make polite requests and refuse or postpone with tact.
Present your education and experience, answer common interview questions with examples, talk about contract benefits and ask good questions at the end of a job interview in Brazilian Portuguese.
Read newspaper headlines and short news items, say where information comes from, report what the news says with the right verbs and understand social media posts and comments in Brazilian Portuguese.

Say where in Brazil people live and come from, describe the main festivals (Carnaval, festa junina and São João, Círio de Nazaré), talk about regional food, words and accents with respect, and understand a short personal text about them.

grupos.titulo: Living in Brazil: bank, CPF, SUS, Pix and documents
grupos.objetivo: Ask clearly what documents and steps you need at a bank, a health clinic, a phone shop or a rental agency, understand the key words (CPF, RNM, Pix, SUS, boleto, contrato) and make polite requests, knowing that procedures change and must always be checked with the institution itself.

grupos.titulo: Strategies: paraphrasing, asking for help, registers and slang
grupos.objetivo: Keep a conversation going when a word is missing (describe, paraphrase, ask for help, check understanding), choose between formal and informal registers, and recognize and use everyday words such as «legal», «massa», «beleza», «valeu», «tá bom», «né» and «cara», knowing that they vary by region.

grupos.titulo: Prepositions and crase: the grave accent «à»
grupos.objetivo: Choose the preposition that each common verb requires (often different from English), write the grave accent «à» correctly with a simple two-step test, and use the prepositions of time and place in both the written and the spoken norm.

Choose the right tense or mood for a sentence (present, perfeito, imperfeito, mais-que-perfeito, perfeito composto, the futures, the three subjunctives, the conditional and the imperative) by asking when, how real and how complete the action is, and use all of them together in a short story.

grupos.titulo: B1 simulado: listening, reading, grammar, speaking and writing
grupos.objetivo: Check your B1 level honestly in four sessions: understand a text and a conversation, apply grammar and vocabulary, plan and judge a written and a spoken task with a self-check list, and solve a scored mixed set of 24 items. The simulado is Linvuu's own self-assessment and is not equivalent to any external exam.
